name: Power Metal
about: Power metal takes the speed of Helloween's early records and the melody of Iron Maiden and Queen and aims them at the sky: clean, high tenor vocals, twin harmony leads, double-bass drumming, major-key choruses and lyrics about dragons, battles and Tolkien. The European strain was born in Hamburg with Helloween's Keeper of the Seven Keys albums in 1987 and 1988 and spread through Blind Guardian, Gamma Ray, Stratovarius and Italy's Rhapsody, who added symphonic bombast. The American version, from Manowar, Manilla Road and Cirith Ungol to Iced Earth, is darker and heavier, closer to its NWOBHM roots. Long mocked for its earnestness, the style has a devoted international audience, and Sabaton, Powerwolf and Unleash the Archers now headline festivals.

artists.name: Helloween
artists.why: the Keeper albums made the style

albums.title: Crystal Logic
albums.why: Mark Shelton's Wichita band found their epic voice on their third album, with Necropolis and the title track as the foundation stones of American power metal.

albums.title: Hail to England
albums.why: Recorded in six days, Manowar's third album is their leanest and heaviest, with Blood of My Enemies and Joey DeMaio's bass solo; absurd and glorious.

albums.title: King of the Dead
albums.why: Tim Baker's wail and Michael Whelan's cover art on a doom-tinged epic metal record that was ignored in its day and canonised decades later.

albums.title: Keeper of the Seven Keys Part I
albums.why: Michael Kiske's debut with the band and the thirteen-minute Halloween set out the European power metal formula: speed, melody and a big, bright chorus.

albums.title: Hall of the Mountain King
albums.why: The Oliva brothers' breakthrough, with Criss Oliva's riffs and a Grieg adaptation, is the best of the US bands' heavier, more theatrical take on the style.

albums.title: Keeper of the Seven Keys Part II
albums.why: Eagle Fly Free, I Want Out and the title epic made this the definitive power metal album, and the Hansen-Weikath-Kiske line-up never recorded together again.

albums.title: Transcendence
albums.why: Midnight's four-octave voice and the masked Florida band's progressive edge on an album that fans of both Queensrÿche and Helloween claim.

albums.title: Death or Glory
albums.why: Rock'n'Rolf's pirate metal at its tightest, with Riding the Storm and Bad to the Bone, the Hamburg band's most consistent album.

albums.title: Night of the Stormrider
albums.why: Jon Schaffer's triplet riffing and a concept about damnation on the album that defined the American strain, heavier and more thrash-indebted than Europe's.

albums.title: Land of the Free
albums.why: Kai Hansen took back the microphone and wrote his most focused set since Helloween, with Rebellion in Dreamland as the genre's great slow-build opener.

albums.title: Imaginations from the Other Side
albums.why: The Krefeld band's turn from speed metal to layered, choral epics peaks with the title track and Bright Eyes, Hansi Kürsch at the height of his powers.

albums.title: Holy Land
albums.why: Andre Matos's São Paulo band folded Brazilian rhythms and orchestral writing into power metal, a record with no real precedent in the genre.

albums.title: Visions
albums.why: Timo Tolkki's neoclassical runs and Timo Kotipelto's tenor on the Finnish band's best-known album, with Black Diamond as its signature song.

albums.title: Glory to the Brave
albums.why: The Gothenburg band's debut revived old-fashioned heavy metal at the height of grunge and nu metal, and sold enough to start a wave of imitators.

albums.title: Symphony of Enchanted Lands
albums.why: Luca Turilli's film-score orchestration, Fabio Lione's operatic voice and a fantasy saga on the album that invented symphonic power metal in full.

albums.title: Nightfall in Middle-Earth
albums.why: The Silmarillion as a concept album, with spoken interludes and Mirror Mirror; dense, overwrought and the genre's most ambitious record.

albums.title: Oceanborn
albums.why: Tarja Turunen's operatic soprano and Tuomas Holopainen's keyboards on the Finnish band's second album, the bridge from power metal to symphonic metal.

albums.title: Ecliptica
albums.why: Tony Kakko's Kemi band debuted with FullMoon and a glossier, more romantic take on Stratovarius's sound, the start of Finland's second wave.

albums.title: Theater of Salvation
albums.why: Tobias Sammet's Fulda band at their most serious, before the humour took over, with the title epic as evidence of how good they could be.

albums.title: Awakening the World
albums.why: Daniel Heiman's voice is the attraction on this Swedish cult record, a slice of pure, grandiose power metal that collectors trade at a premium.

albums.title: The Black Halo
albums.why: Roy Khan's Faust-inspired concept, with guests from Epica and Dimmu Borgir, is the most sophisticated American power metal album of its decade.

albums.title: Inhuman Rampage
albums.why: Through the Fire and Flames made DragonForce the video-game generation's power metal band; relentlessly fast, deliberately silly, hard to resist.

albums.title: Carolus Rex
albums.why: The Swedish band's concept album about their country's empire, recorded in both Swedish and English, is their most coherent and the one that filled arenas.

albums.title: Apex
albums.why: Brittney Slayes's voice and a sci-fi narrative on the Vancouver band's fourth album, the strongest case that power metal still has new things to say.
